   interactions, history, files.

  (see the `959831c` entry) — concrete, with file references, not vague.
- **`architecture.md`** — if the mechanics changed (a new hook, a changed guard pattern, the
  ticket 02 `mtg-card` rewrite landing). Keep the "How to tell this owner's territory from
  `two-faced-cards`'s" section accurate if the file split changes.
- **`interactions.md`** — if a new watch point emerged, or an existing one's file/line references
  moved. Watch point 1 (the `onClick` selection-deferral quirk) should stay watch point 1 as long
  as it's the single most likely regression — don't bury it.

  ticket 02's rewrite lands — expect to rewrite most of this file then).
- **`README.md`** — only if the charge itself shifted (unlikely for a routine fix) or the scope
  genuinely expanded (e.g. a second custom shape type joins the Tabletop).

Commit the KB updates with a message tagged `- claude`. Keep the commit focused on the KB changes
— don't bundle in unrelated app-code fixes.

1 --- 2 name: tabletop-shape-mechanics 3 kind: capability 4 --- 5 6 # Tabletop Shape Mechanics 7 8 **The charge**: every gesture on a Tabletop card — tap, drag, drop — must act on the shape 9 actually under the pointer, using tldraw's own selection/translation state machine correctly, 10 even where that state machine has surprising edge cases around custom `ShapeUtil` hooks. This 11 holds regardless of what a shape displays (card face, furniture, future shape types); it's about 12 the *mechanics* of clicking and dragging things on the canvas, not what they look like. 13 14 This capability isn't user-visible as a feature — a player just expects "the card I dragged is 15 the card that moves." But when it breaks, it's a *glaring* bug (see `history.md`, `959831c`): 16 drag one card, then drag another, and the wrong one moves. That's the kind of failure this owner 17 exists to prevent from recurring, and to catch when someone else's change reopens it. 18 19 ## Why this owner exists 20 21 Born 2026-08-07 out of a bug fix (`959831c`, "drag picks up the wrong card after a previous 22 drag"). The finding — a genuine tldraw quirk in its `SelectTool` state machine — initially landed 23 in `owners/two-faced-cards/` purely because that owner's trigger was broad enough to match "the 24 Tabletop's card rendering." It has nothing to do with card faces, flip, or `CardDefinition`. Jess 25 called out that shape-selection mechanics is complex enough to deserve its own standing owner, so 26 future bugs in this territory route here instead of being caught incidentally by a 27 card-rendering owner. See `history.md` for the full migration note. 28 29 ## Scope 30 31 Everything under `apps/tabletop/src/client/shapes/` — `MtgCardShapeUtil.tsx`, 32 `MtgZoneShapeUtil.tsx`, `MtgCounterShapeUtil.tsx`, `MtgCounterTool.ts`, plus the pure seams 33 `zoneHitTest.ts` and `openSpotNearZoneEdge.ts` — and their interaction with tldraw's own 34 `SelectTool` child states (`PointingShape`, `Translating`, in 35 `node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/tools/SelectTool/childStates/`). 36 Concretely: click/tap toggling, drag-and-drop (including drag-and-drop *parenting* — counters 37 attaching to cards), shape selection state, zone detection via shape bounds, custom creation 38 tools, and any tldraw quirk discovered while implementing these. 39 40 **Ticket 02/12** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/12-*.md`, landed 2026-08-08) carried out the 41 rewrite decided by ticket 02: the card is now a genuine custom shape type, `mtg-card`, defined in 42 `apps/tabletop/src/shared/mtgCardShape.ts` and rendered by `MtgCardShapeUtil` extending 43 `BaseBoxShapeUtil` (not `ImageShapeUtil`). The old `MtgCardImageShapeUtil.tsx` is deleted. 44 45 **Ticket 13** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/13-*.md`, landed 2026-08-08) did the same for 46 furniture: the playmat, library, graveyard, exile, and the Stack are now a genuine custom shape 47 type, `mtg-zone`, defined in `apps/tabletop/src/shared/mtgZoneShape.ts` and rendered by 48 `MtgZoneShapeUtil` extending `BaseBoxShapeUtil`. Furniture is **no longer** "stock locked 49 `geo`/`image` shapes with no custom ShapeUtil" — that was true before this ticket, isn't now. 50 `MtgZoneShapeUtil` defines no interaction hooks at all (see `architecture.md`), which makes it 51 the KB's working example of "a locked shape needs none." See `architecture.md` for the mechanics 52 and the tldraw registration gotchas both rewrites surfaced. 53 54 **Ticket 17** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/17-flip-and-face-down.md`, landed 2026-08-09, 55 `eb24a4f`/`ff5d58a`) added the app's **first custom tldraw `ContextMenu`** — 56 `apps/tabletop/src/client/CardContextMenu.tsx`, wired via `TLComponents.ContextMenu` in 57 `TablePage.tsx` — carrying Flip/Turn face-down/Tap-Untap menu items for `mtg-card`. Mechanics 58 territory here is narrow but real: right-clicking a card selects it exactly like `PointingShape` 59 does, and unlike a locked shape's selection (which tldraw clears when the context menu closes), 60 an **unlocked card's selection survives menu close** — reopening watch point 1's stale-selection 61 hazard through a second gesture besides drag. See `architecture.md`'s "Ticket 17" section and 62 watch point 15. 63 64 **Ticket 18** (`.scratch/tabletop-physics/issues/18-counters.md`, landed 2026-08-08, `4c64ef2`) 65 added a third custom shape type: `mtg-counter`, an **unlocked, draggable, text-editable disc** 66 a player drops onto a card. Attachment is tldraw drag-and-drop *parenting*, mediated by drag 67 hooks on `mtg-card` (`canReceiveNewChildrenOfType`/`onDragShapesIn`/`onDragShapesOut`); a card 68 entering graveyard/exile/library evicts its counters to open spots near the zone's edge. 69 **Naming caution**: table-layout ticket 12's decided-but-unbuilt life counter also used the 70 working name `mtg-counter` — ticket 18 claimed the type string per the tabletop-physics spec, 71 so the life counter is named `mtg-life-counter` instead. 212	## Right-click context menu goes dead after one dismiss-by-outside-click cycle — `@tldraw/editor`'s `MenuClickCapture` desyncs Radix's own open state (2026-08-19)
213	
214	TODO.md bug: "In tabletop, often after selecting a card, I right-click and the menu comes up...
215	once. After that, right-clicking does nothing... until doing a bunch of unrelated things."
216	
217	**Root cause, found by reading `node_modules/@tldraw/editor/src/lib/components/MenuClickCapture.tsx`
218	(baked into `DefaultCanvas`, not overridable via `TLComponents` — a new fact for this KB, see
219	below), not guessed.** Tldraw's `DefaultContextMenu` is built on Radix's `ContextMenu.Root`, which
220	owns its own internal open/closed boolean and only transitions it through its own handshake
221	(`onOpenChange`, or its own Escape/outside-pointerdown detection). Whenever `tlmenus.hasAnyOpenMenus()`
222	is true, `MenuClickCapture` renders a full-canvas capture `div` so an outside click doesn't also
223	hit the canvas underneath. For a plain **left-button** outside click, its `handlePointerDown`
224	closes the menu by calling `editor.menus.clearOpenMenus()` **directly** — bypassing Radix's own
225	close path entirely. That clears tldraw's `tlmenus` atom, so `DefaultContextMenu`'s conditionally-
226	rendered `Portal` unmounts and the menu visually disappears — but Radix's own internal `open` state
227	inside `ContextMenu.Root` is never told to close. On the *next* right-click, Radix sees its own
228	state already `open: true` and no-ops (never calls `onOpenChange` again), so `tlmenus` never gets
229	re-added and the menu silently fails to reopen — while shape selection on right-click, a completely
230	separate code path (`SelectTool`'s `Idle.onRightClick` state-chart handling), is unaffected, which
231	is exactly why the card visibly selects while the menu stays gone. Confirmed empirically: dismissing
232	via **Escape** (which DOES go through Radix's own dismissable-layer handshake) never desyncs and can
233	be repeated indefinitely; dismissing via an outside **left-click** desyncs it after exactly one
234	cycle, every time.
235	
236	**`rightClickPanning` was tried first and ruled out as a red herring** — it governs whether a
237	right-click *opens* panning vs. the context menu, unrelated to this bug, which lives entirely on
238	the menu's *close-via-outside-click* path. The app stays on tldraw's default `rightClickPanning: true`,
239	unchanged.
240	
241	**New KB fact: `MenuClickCapture` is baked into `DefaultCanvas` and is NOT swappable via
242	`TLComponents`** — unlike `ContextMenu` itself (watch point 15/`CardContextMenu.tsx`, ticket 17),
243	there is no component-override seam for this piece. Any future fix touching it has to work around
244	it from outside, not replace it.
245	
246	**Fix**: `apps/tabletop/src/client/closeContextMenuBeforeOutsideClick.ts` (new) — a document-level
247	**capture-phase** `pointerdown` listener, registered from `onTldrawMount` in `TablePage.tsx`
248	alongside the existing `clearStaleSelectionOnPointerDown(editor)` call. Capture phase is load-bearing:
249	it must run *before* `MenuClickCapture`'s own React (bubble-phase) handler. When a menu is open and
250	the click is left-button and lands **outside** the menu's own DOM (`[data-testid="context-menu"]`),
251	it dispatches a synthetic `Escape` keydown on `document` — Radix's own dismissable-layer listens for
252	that and runs its correct close handshake. By the time `MenuClickCapture.handlePointerDown` runs its
253	`clearOpenMenus()` afterward, the menu is already closed and in sync, so that call is a no-op instead
254	of a desync. Clicks landing on the menu itself (choosing a menu item) are explicitly excluded, or the
255	injected Escape would cancel the click before its own `onSelect` ever fires.
256	
257	`onTldrawMount` now returns a cleanup function (`closeContextMenuBeforeOutsideClick()`'s return
258	value) — `<Tldraw onMount={...}>` supports a returned teardown, previously unused by this file since
259	`clearStaleSelectionOnPointerDown` never needed one.
260	
261	**Test**: `apps/tabletop/test/verification/verify-rightclick-reopen.spec.ts` (new, stays as a
262	regression guard) — two tests, both opening/dismissing/reopening the menu 5 times in a loop: one
263	dismissing via Escape (passed even pre-fix, proving the Escape path was never broken), one via an
264	outside left-click (failed after the first cycle pre-fix — the menu simply never reappeared — passes
265	after). Full `./verify.sh` and `npx vitest run` both green.
266	
267	This is a **new entry point into stale-tldraw-internal-state territory, but NOT a member of watch
268	point 1's stale-*selection* family** — watch point 1 is about tldraw's own selection atom outliving
269	a gesture; this bug is about Radix's *own* internal open-state, a third-party library's state, going
270	out of sync with tldraw's `tlmenus` atom. Recorded as a new, separate watch point (26) rather than
271	folded into watch point 15, which is about a card's selection surviving menu close, not about the
272	menu itself failing to reopen.
